advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a malformed/unreadable config causing ConfigError makes `project_applies_to_globs` fall back to the routing `applies_to` (fail open).
evidence: docstring at registry.py:270-272: 'Malformed config deliberately fails OPEN to the routing default (and is logged)'
docs/config.md: 'Malformed config fails open to the declared globs (and is logged) so an unreadable optional key can never silently delete review coverage.'
ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py — `_write_overlay` only ever writes well-formed TOML (line 182-186); no test induces ConfigError.
registry.py:287-296: `table = getattr(composed, section, None); if table is None or not hasattr(table, key): logger.warning(...); return []`
test at tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py:249-255 calls `criteria_overlay._validate_routing_entry(...)` — the shape check, not `_config_globs` runtime resolution
ABSENCE: no test constructs a routing entry whose `applies_to_config_key` passes shape validation but points at a nonexistent config key and asserts the runtime fallback to routing globs.
advisory.finding: The documented fail-open-on-ConfigError contract in `_config_globs` (an unreadable/malformed config must fall back to the declared `applies_to` globs and log a warning) is untested. No test writes a malformed `rebar.toml` or otherwise triggers `_config.ConfigError`, so a regression that let a config parse error silently delete review coverage (fail closed) would not be caught.
merged_from: The runtime 'applies_to_config_key names no config key' fallback path in `_config_globs` (lines 287-296) is untested. `test_malformed_applies_to_config_key_is_a_located_load_error` only exercises the SHAPE validator `_validate_routing_entry`, not the runtime resolution where a shape-valid `<section>.<key>` pointer resolves to a missing section/attribute and must fall back to the declared globs with a logged warning.
scenarios: A project's rebar.toml has a syntax error; the ci-gate-compat criterion should still run with its shipped globs but a fail-closed regression would silently drop it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Write a rebar.toml with invalid TOML under tmp_path and assert `project_applies_to_globs('project.gated', str(tmp_path))` returns the routing globs (and optionally assert a warning is logged via caplog).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that an explicitly empty `ci_config_globs` config value falls back to the routing `applies_to` globs.
evidence: registry.py:309-313: `if isinstance(config_key, str) and config_key: override = _config_globs(...); if override: return override; return _str_globs(entry.get('applies_to'))`
ABSENCE: no test sets `ci_config_globs = []` in config and asserts the routing `applies_to` still applies.
advisory.finding: The empty-config-override fallback branch in `project_applies_to_globs` (`if override:` at line 311, i.e. config key set but resolves to an empty list) is untested. `test_config_key_replaces_the_declared_globs` only uses a non-empty override, so the branch where an empty configured list falls back to the routing `applies_to` is not exercised.
scenarios: A project declares `[code_review] ci_config_globs = []` explicitly; per the docs the routing default should still apply, but the empty-override fallback branch has no test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Call `_write_overlay(tmp_path, routing=_GATED, config_globs=[])` and assert `project_applies_to_globs('project.gated', str(tmp_path))` equals the routing globs.
